summary: Built everything the flood views read beyond the list. M1 sources: NOAA water maps (RFC forecast flooded area with the layer-3 reach join so the area figure counts only the flood's own gauges' reaches, CatFIM, National Water Model maps, river lines), FEMA NFHL (1 % floodplain, floodway and 0.2 % band only; availability from layer 0, effective dates from layer 3; 4 tries and an outage memory), NASA OPERA (measured DSWx-HLS from Earthdata GIS without a login, locked to one pass; CMR and the PO.DAAC token path tested with a fake token and a mock transport; GIBS picture fallback) and USGS water data v1 (no key, USGS_429). M2 bundle: floods/build.py builds a light flood bundle (terrain, NAIP, NWS forecast area, FEMA floodplain, satellite classes, model area, frozen NWS products, gauges with series, satellite PNG) in a staging folder swapped in at the end; POST build and the files route. M3 routes: maps, model, satellite (+ PNG), official flood alerts (zones on demand, at most 20, then counties) and river gauges (members from NWPS, nearby and area gauges from the riv_gauges envelope, never an NWPS list), local alerts and evacuations with hazard=flood (Oregon's wildfire-only feed answers not-available; Cal OES event_type verbatim; the fire default unchanged); fixture-flood answered by the real API from its bundle. Checked on real data (port 8753, FIRE3D_LIVE=0): every route contract-valid for fixture-flood and three real floods; real bundles built through POST build in 36 s cold (St. Johns River, FL, 17.7 MB) and 15-24 s warm (Peace River, FL, 17.6 MB).

known_issues: Earthdata GIS lags NASA's archive and Landsat swaths leave tiles half empty: some floods have no usable measured pass in the last 10 days and get the GIBS picture (measured false, SAT_NO_IMAGE). Cloudy areas get a heavily hatched image (Peace River: 89.6 % cloud).

The EARTHDATA_TOKEN path (PO.DAAC download, DSWx-S1 class mapping) is untested with a real token (fake token and mock transport only). DSWx-S1 values other than 0, 1, 2, 254, 255 are mapped by reading of the product description (3 -> partial water, masks -> no view).

Past times are not served yet for flood-alerts (ALERTS_PAST_NOT_YET) and river gauges (GAUGES_PAST_NOT_YET): backend-flood-live M2 adds the IEM archive and USGS history (usgs_water.observed_series is ready).
A nearby gauge's forecast is null unless rfc_max_forecast lists it; ?lid= gives it exactly. The web should not say NO_RFC_FORECAST when is_forecast_point is true.
Point queries (flood-alerts?bbox=, river-gauges?bbox=) at the fixture's place answer real NWS / NOAA data (no synthetic data in real answers); the demo's point check should use ?flood=fixture-flood.
FEMA zones over a 60 km Florida area are about 13,600 polygons (6 MB, 1.1 MB gzipped; 10 s cold, then cached 30 days). More than 20,000 would be cut with NFHL_TRUNCATED.
Cold NWM 5-day maps over a 60 km area can take about 30 s (many polygons); cached 6 h.
The bundle's GeoJSON copies leave out polygons smaller than one render cell (59 m at 60 km) to stay under 20 MB; the rasters and the 2D routes use the full answers.
The satellite route caches its answer 30 min per flood; the bundle's satellite.json is refreshed only by a rebuild (backend-flood-live queues refreshes).
The flood live loop, auto-build and status from the loop are backend-flood-live's; nothing here starts a background task.
My scratch folder holds request caches and copies of public satellite PNGs only (no secrets).
